title: Nylon-Tokenizer: Hardware-Aligned Byte-Level BPE with Domain-Aware Pretokenization for Compact Language Models
subtitle: Co-designing subword vocabularies strictly to V = 65,536 for native uint16 serialization, halving 120B pretraining token storage to 240 GB.
abstract: Subword tokenization is a foundational architectural interface in autoregressive language models, dictating the trade-off between sequence length, vocabulary embedding parameter volume, and pretraining data storage. We present Nylon-Tokenizer, an open byte-level Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) system co-designed around the systems and workload constraints of compact language models (≤ 1.5B parameters). Nylon-Tokenizer combines hardware-aligned token storage at the exact V = 65,536 boundary, domain-aware pretokenization, and affected-sequence BPE induction.

title: Nylon V1: 338M Autoregressive Pretraining and Preference Alignment
subtitle: Training a 337.96M parameter transformer on 5.36B tokens across 2× RTX 5090s with Supervised Fine-Tuning and Direct Preference Optimization.
abstract: We release Nylon V1, a 337.96M parameter autoregressive language model pretrained from scratch across 5.36 billion tokens on dual NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 GPUs in 34h 22m. The model sustained 41,161 tokens/sec throughput over 155,441 steps, converging to a validation loss of 2.1804 (8.8498 perplexity). We subsequently align the checkpoint through a 2-stage post-training pipeline: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) over 283.7M tokens (validation perplexity 3.0042) and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO, beta=0.1) across 8,841 steps, yielding open-weights deployed via Ollama and Hugging Face.
